name: KinStudy Offline Knowledge Base
description: Essential Mathematics formulas and Science laws for instant offline study lookup

entries.title: Quadratic Formula
entries.explanation: Finds the solutions (roots or x-intercepts) for any quadratic equation of the form ax² + bx + c = 0.
entries.analogy: Think of the discriminant (b² - 4ac) as a traffic signal: positive means two real crossroads (2 real solutions), zero means exactly one touchpoint, and negative means you're flying above the ground with imaginary numbers!
stepByStep: Write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0
Identify coefficients a, b, and c
Compute the discriminant: D = b² - 4ac
Substitute into x = (-b ± √D) / (2a)
Calculate both values (+ and -)

entries.title: Pythagorean Theorem
entries.explanation: In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse (the longest side opposite the right angle) is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
entries.analogy: Imagine walking across a rectangular park diagonally instead of taking the two perpendicular sidewalks. The square of your diagonal shortcut equals the sum of the squares of the sidewalk paths!
stepByStep: Verify the triangle has a 90-degree right angle
Identify legs 'a' and 'b', and hypotenuse 'c' (opposite the 90° angle)
Square both legs: a² and b²
Add the squares: a² + b²
Take the square root to find c: c = √(a² + b²)
entries.example: A triangle with legs 3 cm and 4 cm: c² = 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 => c = √25 = 5 cm.

entries.title: Slope-Intercept Line Equation
entries.formula: y = mx + b  (where m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁))
entries.explanation: Represents a straight line on the Cartesian plane where 'm' is the steepness (slope) and 'b' is where the line crosses the vertical y-axis.
entries.analogy: Think of 'b' as your starting altitude at ground zero (x=0), and 'm' as how many meters you climb for every step forward you take.
stepByStep: Find the slope m = (y₂ - y₁) / (x₂ - x₁)
Locate where the line crosses the y-axis to find b
Combine into y = mx + b to predict any y for any given x
entries.example: Line passing through (0, 3) with a slope of 2: y = 2x + 3. At x = 4, y = 2(4) + 3 = 11.

entries.title: Circle Area and Circumference
entries.explanation: Area calculates the total 2D surface inside a circle; Circumference measures the perimeter or distance around the outer boundary.
entries.analogy: Circumference is the crust around the outer edge of your pizza pie; Area is all the delicious melted cheese and toppings spread across the top!
stepByStep: Measure the radius 'r' (distance from center to edge; radius = diameter / 2)
For circumference: multiply radius by 2π (approx 6.283)
For area: square the radius (r × r) and multiply by π (approx 3.14159)
entries.example: Radius = 7 cm: Circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 7 = 44 cm. Area = (22/7) × 7² = 154 cm².

entries.title: Newton's Second Law of Motion
entries.explanation: The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting upon it and inversely proportional to its mass. Force is measured in Newtons (N).
entries.analogy: Pushing an empty shopping cart (low mass) makes it accelerate quickly with a light shove. Pushing a cart loaded with 100 books requires massive force just to get it moving at the same speed!
stepByStep: Identify the mass of the object in kilograms (kg)
Measure or define acceleration in meters per second squared (m/s²)
Multiply mass by acceleration: F = m × a (result in Newtons)
entries.example: A 1000 kg car accelerates at 3 m/s²: Net Force = 1000 kg × 3 m/s² = 3,000 Newtons.

entries.title: Kinetic & Gravitational Potential Energy
entries.formula: KE = ½ m v²  |  PE = m · g · h
entries.explanation: Potential energy is stored energy due to height (position in a gravitational field); Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses due to its motion.
entries.analogy: At the very top of a roller coaster drop, you are packed with maximum Potential Energy. As you plummet down, that stored energy transforms directly into roaring Kinetic speed!
stepByStep: For Potential Energy: PE = mass (kg) × gravity (9.8 m/s²) × height (meters)
For Kinetic Energy: square velocity (v²), multiply by mass, divide by 2
Total Mechanical Energy is conserved: Total = KE + PE
entries.example: A 2 kg ball lifted 5 meters high: PE = 2 × 9.8 × 5 = 98 Joules. When it hits the ground, that 98 J has converted into KE.

entries.title: Ohm's Law of Electricity
entries.explanation: States that the electrical current flowing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points and inversely proportional to resistance.
entries.analogy: Imagine water flowing through a garden pipe: Voltage is the water pressure pushing from the tap, Current is the volume of water flowing per second, and Resistance is someone squeezing the hose!
stepByStep: Voltage (V) in Volts
Current (I) in Amperes
Resistance (R) in Ohms (Ω)
Rearrange as needed: V = I·R, I = V / R, or R = V / I
entries.example: A 12V battery connected to a 4Ω resistor: Current I = 12 / 4 = 3 Amperes.

entries.title: Chemical Equation of Photosynthesis
entries.explanation: The process by which green plants and certain organisms transform light energy into chemical energy, converting carbon dioxide and water into glucose sugar and releasing oxygen gas.
entries.analogy: Plants are nature's solar-powered bakeries! They take in stale air (CO₂) and water from their roots, use sunlight as the oven's power, and bake sweet sugar (glucose) while giving us clean oxygen to breathe!
stepByStep: Reactants: 6 molecules of Carbon Dioxide (6CO₂) + 6 molecules of Water (6H₂O)
Energy Driver: Photons captured by green chlorophyll pigment
Products: 1 molecule of Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) + 6 molecules of Oxygen (6O₂)
entries.example: Without this equation, Earth's atmospheric oxygen would deplete and the food chain's primary producers would vanish.

entries.title: Ideal Gas Law
entries.explanation: Relates pressure (P), volume (V), amount of substance in moles (n), the ideal gas constant (R), and absolute temperature in Kelvin (T).
entries.analogy: Think of gas molecules as hyperactive bouncing balls in a box. If you shrink the box (lower V) or heat up the room (higher T), they slam against the walls much faster and harder, skyrocketing the pressure (P)!
stepByStep: Always convert Temperature to Kelvin: K = °C + 273.15
Use universal gas constant R = 8.314 J/(mol·K) or 0.0821 L·atm/(mol·K)
Isolate target variable: e.g., P = (nRT) / V
entries.example: 1 mole of gas at STP (0°C = 273.15 K, 1 atm pressure) occupies exactly 22.4 Liters of volume.

entries.title: Density Formula
entries.explanation: A measure of how much matter is packed into a given unit of space. Objects with density less than water (1.0 g/cm³) float, while denser objects sink.
entries.analogy: A shoebox packed with feathers and an identical shoebox packed with solid lead bricks have the exact same volume, but the lead box has vastly higher density!
stepByStep: Measure the mass 'm' using a digital balance (in grams or kilograms)
Measure the volume 'V' using geometry or water displacement (cm³ or m³)
Divide mass by volume: ρ = m / V
entries.example: A metal cube with mass 270g and volume 100cm³: Density = 270 / 100 = 2.7 g/cm³ (this matches the density of Aluminum!).

entries.title: Kinematics: Velocity & Acceleration
entries.formula: v = d / t  |  a = (v_final - v_initial) / t
entries.explanation: Velocity is the rate of change of position with direction; Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity over time.
entries.analogy: Speed is reading 60 mph on your speedometer. Velocity is 60 mph heading strictly North. Acceleration is slamming the gas pedal to surge from 0 to 60 mph in 3 seconds!
stepByStep: Average Speed: Divide total distance traveled by total time taken
Acceleration: Subtract initial velocity from final velocity and divide by elapsed time
entries.example: A cyclist speeds up from 2 m/s to 8 m/s in 3 seconds: Acceleration = (8 - 2) / 3 = 2 m/s².

entries.title: Trigonometric Ratios (SOH CAH TOA)
entries.formula: sin(θ) = Opp/Hyp | cos(θ) = Adj/Hyp | tan(θ) = Opp/Adj
entries.explanation: The fundamental ratios connecting the angles of a right triangle to the lengths of its sides.
entries.analogy: Remember the classic mnemonic: Some Old Horses Can Always Hear Their Owners Approach (SOH CAH TOA)!
stepByStep: Identify the reference angle θ
Label the sides: Hypotenuse (longest), Opposite (facing θ), Adjacent (next to θ)
Pick ratio based on what you have and what you need to solve
entries.example: In a 3-4-5 right triangle with angle θ facing the 3 side: sin(θ) = 3/5 = 0.6, cos(θ) = 4/5 = 0.8, tan(θ) = 3/4 = 0.75.
